page: Amazon Web Services m7g.xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton processor family. It features 4 dedicated physical cores built on the 64-bit ARM64 architecture, specifically utilizing the Neoverse-V1 model running at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the m7g.xlarge in the average performance tier for most standard compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside Geekbench scores, demonstrate mid-range capabilities. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 386.52 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 102.9 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The server handles static web serving at 8.15 GB/sec and processes 6.65 million Redis SET operations per second. However, performance drops to weak or poor tiers in specific workloads, such as bzip3 decompression, Geekbench ray tracing, and Passmark encryption tests. Large language model inference speeds are also limited, with text generation on a 7B model yielding only 6.03 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides a resource-dense profile for general-purpose workloads without the premium associated with x86 hardware. The absence of local storage and dedicated GPUs makes it a streamlined option for stateless applications. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, text processing, and general-purpose application hosting where extreme cryptographic or floating-point performance is not required.
description: Amazon Web Services m7g.xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by a 2.6 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor with 4 dedicated ARM64 physical cores and 16.0 GB of memory. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance lacks local storage and features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates average performance for standard tasks, including static web serving at 8.15 GB/sec and 6.65 million Redis SET operations per second. However, it exhibits performance trade-offs, showing weak results in encryption, bzip3 decompression, and LLM inference. The server offers a resource-dense, qualitatively cost-efficient profile for stateless applications. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, text processing, database operations, and web serving.
